children: By Mariapaula Gonzalez
September is notoriously tough on the stock market, but investors might be able to exhale now that Labor Day is here.

Earlier this year, artificial intelligence helped spur a market rally that lifted the S&P 500 higher-but those gains have dwindled under the weight of rising borrowing costs, making the past few weeks tough on investors.

As summer winds down and pumpkin spice takes over, investors may be taking time to relax over the holiday weekend following August's earnings rush. Here's what you should know about trading hours on Monday.
Is the Stock Market Open or Closed on Labor Day?
Both the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq Stock Market will be closed on Monday in observance of Labor Day before reopening at 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday.
Over-the counter markets and U.S. bond markets will also be shut in observance of the federal holiday, and will reopen at their regular hours on Tuesday.
Are International Markets Open on Labor Day?

The Toronto Stock Exchange will be closed Monday for Canada's Labour Day. However, other foreign exchanges, including the London Stock Exchange, the Shanghai Stock Exchange, and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong will be open.
Are Banks and Post Offices Open Today?
Most banks, including branches at Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo, will be closed. However, ATMs and online banking services will generally be available.
Post offices won't be open. Labor Day is one of 11 U.S. Postal Service holidays observed in 2026, according to the agency's website.
What About Private Carriers?

There is no UPS delivery or pickup service on Monday. Store locations may be closed; the carrier recommends checking with your local store. However, UPS Express Critical, a shipping service for packages requiring extra care, will remain available.

FedEx, meanwhile, will halt most operations on Labor Day. However, some store locations will remain open with modified hours. FedEx Custom Critical, a shipping service handling fragile packages, will also be available.
How Has the Stock Market Performed Around Labor Day?
Over the summer, rising oil prices, expectations of interest-rate hikes, and growing government deficit concerns drove bond yields higher.

That surge reignited fears of a typical September stock slump-a seasonal pattern Wall Street knows all too well. Over the past five and ten years, the S&P 500 has dropped an average of 2.7% and 1.3% during the month, respectively, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
The index, however, rose 2.6% in August-beating its historical 5-year and 10-year average gains of 0.2% and 0.9% for the month, respectively.
What Else Should I Know About Labor Day?
Celebrated annually on the first Monday in September, Labor Day honors the contributions of American workers.
President Grover Cleveland signed a bill that made the tradition a federal holiday law in 1894, after more than 20 states had adopted the occasion as a holiday that year.

Beyond its historical roots, Labor Day also marks the unofficial end of peak hot dog grilling season. Last year, the National Hot Dog and Sausage Council reported that Americans typically consume 7 billion hot dogs from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
